subject: Reschedule request: extra lead time for prompt workflows & sample ingestion
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@finlytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to shift demo — travel & internal prep

Evelyn / Marcus,

Thanks again for setting up next week’s product walkthrough (scheduled for Mon, Aug 10). I need to ask whether we can move it out by one week. Our VP of Data is unexpectedly traveling the 9–11 window and she’s the primary decision-maker for this evaluation.

Separately, our engineering team needs a bit more runway to complete an export of sample workload traces and to sanitize PII — we expect to have the files ready by Aug 12. If we keep the demo on Aug 10 we won’t be able to validate the traces with your team beforehand.

Would you be able to reschedule for Aug 17 or Aug 18? Ideally a morning PT slot (between 10:00–13:00 PT). I can also have our platform engineer (Anna) coordinate data upload and staging access — she’s cc’d.

Attached: sample-traces-2026-08-03.csv (small extract).

Appreciate the flexibility — want to make sure we get a productive session where your engineers can exercise our real traces.

Best,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Analytics, Finlytics
Tom.Reynolds@finlytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to shift demo — travel & internal prep

Tom — thanks for the heads up and for the sample extract. Moving is fine; we’d rather have a session where we can validate with your traces.

Operational asks so we can make the most of the extra lead time:
- We need at least 72 hours before the demo to run prompt-set sensitivity tests and a single end-to-end ingest. If you can confirm the full export by Aug 12 that timeline works.
- Please share staging credentials (or a temporary S3 pre-signed upload) and confirm whether the traces contain PII. If there is PII, note the redaction steps you’ll take.
- We’ve put together a short runbook for customers doing sample ingest and prompt validation — link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-runbook (attaching a PDF copy). It lists preferred formats (CSV/NDJSON), expected field names, and a minimal manifest file.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Aug 17, 2026 — 10:00 AM PT (preferred)
- Wed Aug 18, 2026 — 02:00 PM PT

Also recommend a 30-minute dry run with our infra engineer the day before (Aug 16) to validate access and KV-cache behavior. Marcus — looping you in to confirm the dry-run timing and what we’ll need on the Finlytics side.

Attached: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to shift demo — travel & internal prep

Thanks — quick technical note from my side. Small checklist so we don’t hit last-minute issues:
- Access: we need a read-only service account or temporary S3 pre-signed URL to pull the full traces. If Finlytics provides a one-time S3 pre-signed PUT for upload, include the upload manifest (see runbook).
- Format: CSV is fine, but we need timestamps in ISO8601 and a consistent session_id column. If you have NDJSON that maps events->session, that’s even better.
- PII: If traces contain hashed identifiers that’s ok; if they contain raw emails or SSNs please redact before upload. If redaction needs to be done server-side, let us know and we’ll propose a workflow (takes additional time).
- Ingest helpers: I’m attaching a small helper script we use to validate headers/manifest during ingest (ingest-helper.sh). Please have Finlytics run it once and paste output into the confirm email.

Slots: Aug 17 10:00 AM PT works for me. I also support the Aug 16 11:00 AM PT 30-minute dry run.
